To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plasma Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio alone or in combination with FDG-Pet can accurately predict amyloids PET positivity in preclinical Alzheimer’s disease.
plasma Aβ42 levels combined with FDG PET can accurately predict amyloide PET positivity in cognitively normal individuals and patients with mild cognitive impairments.
plasma TP42/40 can be used for screening of brain amyloidosis in preclinical and mild cognitive impairment stages of Alzheimer’s Disease, with an accuracy of 88.1% and an AUC of.88.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective and accurate biomarker for Alzheimer’s disease.
a potential role of plasma Aβ42 and Aβ40 levels to identify subjects at risk of AD.
the development of a non-invasive, low-cost and easily accessible biomarker to identify subjects who are likely to be amyloid-PET positive.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TP42/40 alone or in combination with FDG-Pet could be used as a potential biomarker for Aβ-PET screening in preclinical and mild AD.
plasma Aβ42 levels alone or in combination with FDG-Pet can be considered as an accurate and reliable tool for detecting brain amyloidosis.
TP42/40 alone or combined with a biomarker of neuro-degeneration is a useful tool in the early detection of Alzheimer’s disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plasma Aβ42 alone or combined with neurodegenerative biomarkers may be used to identify Aβ-PET positives, and thus, reduce the number of unnecessary Aβ-PET exams.
the combination of plasma Aβ42 and Aβ40 levels and FDG-PED scores can be used to predict amyloid-Pet positivity with a high accuracy.
plasma Aβ42 and Aβ40 levels alone or combined with the FDG-PET biomarker of neuro-degeneration could accurately predict Aβ-PET results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of plasma biomarkers and FDGPET could be a promising approach for a non-invasive screening tool for Aβ positivity in the preclinical and prodormal AD.
the combination of plasma TP42/40 and FDG-PED scores is the most accurate predictor of brain Aβ positivity, which may facilitate the implementation of Aβ-PED scans in the clinical setting.
plasma Aβ42 and Aβ40 levels alone or combined with a neurodegeneration biomarker are promising candidates for the early detection of AD.
